variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for N times' (two, three, ...) means N pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step and tracked through the shuffle swaps). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%), the robot is holding the cube, regardless of the table list (the held cube is usually still listed at its old position): choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open; the robot holds nothing even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table', which is a cube just released and settling): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube as updated at this step (after a put-down this is the current position of the cube the execution steps showed released); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Always point at target_cube as updated at this step. When target_cube is absent from the resting list at this step (held or still settling), still point at target_cube itself, never at any other listed cube.

fields.name: target_cube
fields.description: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked, at its current table position. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%; the picked cube is the cube listed nearest the gripper's own [y, x] there (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames confirms it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). Then track the picked cube through the shuffle as a written ledger; do not read it off the final list. Step 1: write the pick spot P (the listed cube nearest the gripper at that lowest frame) and the spot where the cube is put back down (the listed cube reappearing beside the gripper when the fingers reopen); call that spot L. Step 2: from that frame onward, write out every STILL FRAME: a frame whose cube list is the same (within a few px) as the frame before it, with every cube on a resting spot, while the gripper is parked raised. Mid-crossing frames (cubes listed off every resting spot) are skipped and never used to decide where L lands. Step 2b: compare each still configuration to the NEXT still configuration, one pair at a time, writing one line for every pair until the pair that ends at the last demonstration frame. Where the two configurations are identical write 'no swap'. Where they differ, exactly two spots changed occupants: write 'swap k: spot X <-> spot Y; L now = ...' (if L is within about 10 px of X write Y, if of Y write X, otherwise unchanged). After the line for the last demonstration frame write 'swaps found: n' and only then stop. Expect commonly three swaps and sometimes one or two; never stop when L happens to be back on P, because a later swap can move it again, including a swap with a cube the gripper never touched. Two consecutive swaps of the same pair return L to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. Step 3: after the last frame, write the listed position in the scene at the start of execution nearest L (within about 10 px). Never write the cube resting on P when P appeared in any swap line: once any swap touched that spot, the cube resting there is a different cube. At every later decision step: the robot always puts the cube back where it picked it, so write the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the carried value. If there is none (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or listed only as 'lifted off the table' while it settles), copy the carried value unchanged. Do not locate it from the gripper position at the reopen frame, nor from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Never relocate to a cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]
fields.annotation: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up, at its current table position. At the first decision step the picked cube is identified in the DEMONSTRATION STEPS by the gripper's own [y, x] at the frame where it is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%: the cube listed nearest that spot (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames and the cube that reappears beside the gripper at put-down confirm it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). The 'picked' label is then carried through the shuffle one swap at a time, the shuffle being read as a sequence of STILL CONFIGURATIONS. A still configuration is a demonstration frame whose cube list is the same (within a few px) as the frame before it, with every cube on a resting spot and the gripper parked raised. Each still configuration is compared with the NEXT still configuration, pair by pair, up to and including the pair that ends at the last demonstration frame. Two consecutive still configurations that are identical are 'no swap'. Two that differ are exactly one swap: the two spots whose occupants changed have EXCHANGED occupants (the frames between them with cubes off every resting spot are mid-crossing frames). If the labelled cube was one of the two movers, it now rests on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never on its own; if it was not a mover, it stays where it is. Mid-crossing frames only show that a swap is happening and are never used to decide where the label lands; arc continuity may confirm which mover is which but never sends a mover back to its own spot. This is applied swap by swap to the last demonstration frame however many swaps occur and whoever the partners are (commonly three, sometimes one or two): two consecutive swaps of the same pair return the labelled cube to its original spot, and a later swap, possibly with a cube the gripper never touched, may move it away again; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. The label is never settled before the last demonstration frame, even when it is back on the pick spot. The cube resting on the original pick position after the shuffle is never chosen by that fact alone: once any swap touched that spot, the cube there is a different cube swapped in. The value is the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step the robot puts the cube back where it picked it, so the value is the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the previous value; if no such cube is listed (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or shown only as a 'lifted off the table' line while it settles), the value is the previous value unchanged. The gripper's position at the reopen frame, 'held in the gripper' coordinates and 'lifted off the table' coordinates are never used to locate it, and the value never moves to a resting cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed grasps. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, write the carried value plus one if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at about height 0.02 and fingers going from 100% to about 46% (or any 'is held in the gripper' line) AND the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers about 46% open (not 100%). Do not require the cube to be missing from the table list; it is usually still listed at its old position. Otherwise, and always when the fingers at the scene are 100% open (even if a cube is listed 'lifted off the table'), copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Count of completed grasps in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at a decision step whose execution steps show the gripper descend to about height 0.02 over the target cube with fingers closing from 100% to about 46% (or any frame saying a cube 'is held in the gripper'), and whose scene at the decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers still about 46% open. The table list at that scene is irrelevant: the held cube may still be listed at its old table position. It never changes at a decision step whose scene shows fingers 100% open, even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table' there. e.g. 2

At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. blue

The old rule located the cube by 'nearest to where it was set down', so when the shuffle swapped cubes the annotated value named the wrong cube while the recorded subgoal pointed at the cube that had actually been picked. On a scene with many cubes and no shuffle, 'vanishes from the table list' also misled, because a different cube under the gripper's shadow drops out of the list while the picked one stays listed until it is lifted. FAILURE: the annotated target_cube disagreed with the recorded pick point, so the memory could not predict the subgoal (SUFFICIENCY) and the value the rule asks for was not what the step warranted (PREDICTABILITY). CHANGE: target_cube holds the [y, x] of the demonstration's picked cube at its current table position. the policy prompt for subgoal
  The required count: 'again' means 1 pick-up; 'for N times' means N pick-ups (two, three, ...). Start in A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube as derived at the first step (the cube the demonstration picked, tracked through the shuffle swaps). The holding rule sent the policy wrong: it demanded that the cube be 'held in the gripper or missing from the table list', but after a grasp the scene usually still lists the cube at its old table position. Replace it with: if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46%, not 100%), the robot is holding the cube -> B: put it down, regardless of the table list. If the fingers are 100% open the robot holds nothing, even when a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table' (that is a cube just released and settling): then if picks_done is below the required count choose A, pointing at the updated target_cube (which, after a put-down, is the cube the execution steps showed released); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required count choose C: press the button to finish. Add: when the execution steps shown contain a cube held and released, A points at that released cube's current position, which is the same as target_cube after the memory update. Drop the clause 'never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube' as a bare prohibition; keep it only as 'point at target_cube as updated at this step'.

refused
  Two steps asked that target_cube never be replaced by the cube seen released in the execution steps, so as to keep the annotated (carried) value. That carried value was wrong only because the first-step derivation ignored the shuffle swaps; in every episode the cube released is the demonstration's cube, so refreshing target_cube from the released cube is consistent with the recorded picks and is kept. One step asked that the point be copied exactly from the scene list; the recorded points differ from the listed positions by a pixel or two, so no exactness rule is added.

history.critique:
field target_cube, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: a three-pick goal with a demonstration whose shuffle moved the picked cube twice, each time with a different partner. First the picked cube traded places with a second cube, so a stranger came to rest exactly on the picked cube's original spot; then the picked cube (now on the second cube's old spot) traded places with a third cube and ended on the third cube's spot, far from where it started. The annotated value was the picked cube's final spot, but a fresh policy wrote the original spot, so the memory was not predictable from the instruction and the first pick went to the wrong cube (PREDICTABILITY of target_cube, and through it SUFFICIENCY of the first subgoal). The rule stays the same in substance but must state the tracking procedure as a chain: for every consecutive pair of shuffle frames, find the cubes whose listed positions changed by more than a few px; each such cube is carried to the changed position closest to the direction it was already travelling, and the picked-cube label travels with it. A swap may be followed by another swap with a different partner, so the picked cube's label can hop through several spots; the number of swaps is not counted and the cube resting on the original pick position after the shuffle is, whenever any swap touched that position, a different cube that was swapped in. The value is the position at the end of the chain, read in the scene at the start of execution. e.g. [107, 174]

field target_cube, POLICY PROMPT
  Same failure: in a demonstration whose shuffle swapped the picked cube once with one neighbour and then again with another, the policy wrote the cube sitting on the original pick position rather than following the chain of swaps, so its memory disagreed with the annotated value and it pointed the first pick at the wrong cube (PREDICTABILITY, then SUFFICIENCY). The instruction must give an explicit per-frame procedure instead of the general 'exchanging places' remark: after locating the picked cube (gripper lowest at about height 0.02, fingers first about 46%, nearest listed cube), go through the demonstration frames one pair at a time. In each pair, cubes whose positions are within a few px are the same cube; the cubes whose positions changed are in motion, and each one is matched to the new position that continues its own arc (closest to where its previous motion was heading), never to the position it started from. A swap is a run of frames in which exactly two listed spots are vacated and, when the list is still again, the same two spots are filled again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. Each time this happens write one ledger line 'swap: spot X <-> spot Y; L now = ...': if L equals X write Y, if L equals Y write X, otherwise L is unchanged. Mid-crossing frames only tell you a swap is happening; never use them to decide where L lands. Continue to the last demonstration frame however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve (two consecutive swaps of the same pair return L to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started). Step 3: after the last frame, write the listed position in the scene at the start of execution nearest L (within about 10 px). Never write the cube resting on P when P appeared in any swap line: once any swap touched that spot, the cube resting there is a different cube. At every later decision step: the robot always puts the cube back where it picked it, so write the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the carried value. If there is none (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or listed only as 'lifted off the table' while it settles), copy the carried value unchanged. Do not locate it from the gripper position at the reopen frame, nor from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Never relocate to a cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]
fields.annotation: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up, at its current table position. At the first decision step the picked cube is identified in the DEMONSTRATION STEPS by the gripper's own [y, x] at the frame where it is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%: the cube listed nearest that spot (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames and the cube that reappears beside the gripper at put-down confirm it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). The 'picked' label is then carried through the shuffle one swap at a time. A swap is a stretch of demonstration frames during which exactly two listed positions leave their resting spots and, when the list is still again, those same two spots are occupied again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. If the labelled cube was one of the two movers, it now rests on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never on its own; if it was not a mover, it stays where it is. Mid-crossing frames only show that a swap is happening and are never used to decide where the label lands; arc continuity may confirm which mover is which but never sends a mover back to its own spot. This is applied swap by swap to the last demonstration frame however many swaps occur and whoever the partners are: two consecutive swaps of the same pair return the labelled cube to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. The cube resting on the original pick position after the shuffle is never chosen by that fact alone: once any swap touched that spot, the cube there is a different cube swapped in. The value is the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step the robot puts the cube back where it picked it, so the value is the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the previous value; if no such cube is listed (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or shown only as a 'lifted off the table' line while it settles), the value is the previous value unchanged. The gripper's position at the reopen frame, 'held in the gripper' coordinates and 'lifted off the table' coordinates are never used to locate it, and the value never moves to a resting cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed grasps. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, write the carried value plus one if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at about height 0.02 and fingers going from 100% to about 46% (or any 'is held in the gripper' line) AND the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers about 46% open (not 100%). Do not require the cube to be missing from the table list; it is usually still listed at its old position. Otherwise, and always when the fingers at the scene are 100% open (even if a cube is listed 'lifted off the table'), copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Count of completed grasps in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at a decision step whose execution steps show the gripper descend to about height 0.02 over the target cube with fingers closing from 100% to about 46% (or any frame saying a cube 'is held in the gripper'), and whose scene at the decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers still about 46% open. The table list at that scene is irrelevant: the held cube may still be listed at its old table position. It never changes at a decision step whose scene shows fingers 100% open, even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table' there. e.g. 2

fields.name: target_colour
fields.description: At the first decision step (memory empty) write the colour word of the cube identified as the picked cube in the demonstration (the listed cube nearest the gripper at the lowest frame where the fingers first read about 46%): 'red', 'blue', 'green', or 'cube' when the list has no colours. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. blue
fields.annotation: The colour word of the cube the demonstration picked up: 'red', 'blue', 'green', or 'cube' when the scene lists cubes without colour. It is fixed at the first decision step as the colour of the listed cube identified as the picked cube in the demonstration (the cube nearest the gripper at the lowest frame where the fingers first read about 46%), and it never changes at any later step. e.g. blue
